scenes.text: A horse had no values. Neither does AI.

scenes.image_prompt: rider on a horse seen from behind, open field, cinematic, no text, letters, numbers, UI
scenes.voice: Someone says technology is never neutral, that AI is built to control. But look at history. We rode a horse.

scenes.image_prompt: windscreen view of a car driving down an open road, cinematic, no text, letters, numbers, UI
scenes.voice: We drove a car. Nobody asked the horse for its values.

scenes.image_prompt: over-the-shoulder pilot in a headset overseeing a holographic delivery-route strategy map with friendly robot units (command-and-conquer view, delivery of value, not war), no text
scenes.voice: Now we're pilots of something new: bots, robots, AI. And we keep asking if the machine is good or bad.
That's the trap. It has no values to argue about. It goes where the pilot points it. Debate the tool all day and you never touch the one thing that matters.
scenes.quote: Technology is|never neutral|because it's not God-given.

steps: What do you want it to do?
scenes.voice: So audit the pilot. What do you want it to do? Who does it affect? Would you sign your name under it?
You're the pilot. Choose like it.
Want to work through those questions with other pilots? Join our Skool community, Delivery Pilot. Link in the description.
